overall_trace.inputs_seen: 6 verbatim Wikipedia summaries: TIER A popular (entropy, game theory, natural selection) + TIER B obscure low-ML-overlap (retting/fiber separation, wave piloting/swell interference, nixtamalization/alkaline maize processing).
overall_trace.reasoning: Run 16-20 found arXiv frontier ML saturates (~21 hits/query) regardless of param/search optimization (Run 20 meta-audit: bottleneck is corpus, not skill/metric). Hypothesis: a BOUNDED encyclopedia corpus with OBSCURE entries from low-ML-overlap fields (textiles, folk navigation, food chemistry) may yield genuinely sparse atoms never paired with ML. Risk: encyclopedia concepts are MORE mature (established knowledge) so popular ones (TIER A) may saturate even worse. So I sample BOTH tiers to compare per-atom paper-hits (the decisive R10/R12 test).
overall_trace.decision: 12 atoms: TIER A {entropy, game theory, natural selection} x2, TIER B {retting, wave piloting, nixtamalization} x2. AGENT 2 will measure per-atom hits; the key question is whether TIER B < TIER A < arXiv(21).
overall_trace.confidence: high - all 6 summaries are real verbatim Wikipedia text with crisp mechanisms
overall_trace.could_be_wrong_if: even obscure encyclopedia mechanisms, once searched as ML-transferable sub-mechanisms, re-broaden to mature literatures (saturation is corpus-independent).
